newsitem.title: ROMANIA: FUEL SHORTAGES ENDANGER ROMANIA FARMING.
newsitem.headline: FUEL SHORTAGES ENDANGER ROMANIA FARMING.

text.p: Fuel shortages caused by a shortage of hard currency to import energy have hit Romania's farming sector, endangering the harvest of valuable crops, a senior agriculture ministry official said on Friday.
"The situation might grow critical if the fuel shortage continues," the senior official said.
Ministry data showed private and state-run farming enterprises received only 11,900 tonnes of diesel oil over September 1-11, or 36 per cent of the 33,000 tonnes needed.

"Fuel stocks in several counties are nil and many have only some 30 to 50 tonnes in store, which is almost nothing," he said, adding that croplands areas in southern Romania were most affected by the fuel shortage.
The farming sector needed around 3,000 tonnes of diesel oil a day to ensure smooth seasonal farm works, the official said,.
An acute hard currency shortage has forced Romania to cut its crude oil imports over the past months and distribution of fuel supplies has been disrupted across the country.

Scant fuel supplies have affected much ongoing agricultural work, especially ploughing and harvesting of sunflower and maize. Lack of funds at heavily-subsidised state farms to purchase the necessary fuel also added to the problem.
Last month, Romania had to broach its strategic fuel reserves to help the farming sector. Some 19,420 tonnes of diesel oil were taken from the National Material Reserves.
In a bid to tackle the crisis the government has set up a fund to ensure hard currency for vital imports of natural gas, crude and fuel oil. But so far the fund failed to produce great results.

"Luckily, maize and sunflower harvesting has just begun. Let's hope losses caused by delays won't be significant," the official said. Data show Romania has so far harvested some 12 percent of its sunflower crop and 5.0 percent of maize.
Ministry estimates put the 1996 maize crop at more than 10 million tonnes, with plans to some export 1.5 million.
This year's sunflower crop is seen at 1.3 million tonnes.
The official said export hopes depended on promises made by the state-run Romanian Oil Company (ROC) to solve the fuel crisis "as soon as possible".
"For us it is vital to have enough fuel in order to complete harvesting without much delay and prepare next year's crops," the official said. -- Adrian Dascalu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
